name: SaaS Revenue Concept Model
description: The Concept Model behind the SaaS Revenue Metrics Information Product: the things a subscription company counts, how they relate, and the moments that drive MRR, ARR, ARPU and NRR.

concepts.name: Prospect
concepts.description: A person or organisation that has shown interest in the product but has not yet purchased.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: has expressed interest but has not yet purchased
examples: Someone who clicked a LinkedIn ad and read the pricing page
A company that booked a demo but has not started a Trial
specialCases: A person on a Trial is still a Prospect until they subscribe to a paid Plan

concepts.name: Customer
concepts.description: A person or organisation that has an active or past paid subscription.
examples: A startup paying monthly for the Starter Plan
A company that cancelled last year
specialCases: A Prospect on a free Trial is not a Customer yet
A Customer who cancels stays a Customer, with no active Subscription

concepts.name: Account
concepts.description: The container that groups one or more users from the same customer and holds their subscription, billing, and usage.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: binds a @{Customer} to their @{Subscription} and usage
examples: The Acme account, holding five users and one Subscription

concepts.name: Trial
concepts.description: A fixed-duration free evaluation period during which a prospect can use the product before committing to a paid plan.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: gives a @{Prospect} time-boxed free access before converting
examples: A 14-day free Trial of the Pro Plan
specialCases: A Trial that Sales extends is still one Trial

concepts.name: Subscription
concepts.description: A recurring commitment by a customer to pay for access to a plan over a billing period.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: binds a @{Customer} to a @{Plan} for a recurring @{Billing Period}
examples: Acme on the monthly Pro Plan, started 1 March
specialCases: An upgrade moves the same Subscription to a new Plan, it does not start a new one
A cancelled Subscription stays active until its Billing Period ends

concepts.name: Plan
concepts.description: A packaged tier of the product with a specific price, feature set, and usage limits.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: defines the price, features, and limits of a @{Subscription}
examples: Starter
Pro
Enterprise

concepts.name: Billing Period
concepts.description: The cadence at which the customer is charged for their subscription (monthly, annual).
examples: Monthly
Annual
specialCases: Is a Billing Period the cadence (monthly) or one actual period (March)? The expert has not ruled yet

concepts.name: Invoice
concepts.description: A bill issued to a customer for a billing period of their subscription.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: records charges owed by a @{Customer} for a @{Billing Period}
examples: The March invoice for Acme's Pro Subscription
specialCases: A prorated upgrade charge goes on the next Invoice, not a new one

concepts.name: Payment
concepts.description: Money received from a customer in settlement of an invoice.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: settles an @{Invoice} with money from a @{Customer}
examples: Acme's card payment for the March invoice

concepts.name: Recurring Revenue
concepts.description: Income recognised from active subscriptions, normalised across customers and plans. The basis for MRR and ARR.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: is generated by active @{Subscription}s on a predictable cadence
examples: Acme's Pro Subscription for March
specialCases: Is Recurring Revenue one amount per Subscription per month, or a running total? It has to be countable to be a Concept

concepts.name: One-Time Revenue
concepts.description: Income from non-recurring sales (setup fees, add-ons, services). Explicitly excluded from MRR / ARR by this information product's scope.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: is not generated by an active @{Subscription}
examples: An onboarding fee
A paid training session

concepts.name: Discount
concepts.description: A reduction applied to a subscription's list price. It is included in revenue calculations, per the IP's scope decisions.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: reduces the price of a @{Subscription} for a @{Customer}
examples: 20% off the first year of the Pro Plan

concepts.name: Channel
concepts.description: A source through which a prospect was first reached (ad, referral, organic, direct).
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: first brought a @{Prospect} to the product
examples: LinkedIn ads
A partner referral
Organic search

concepts.name: Ad
concepts.description: A specific marketing creative run on a channel that prospects may click.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: is the creative a @{Prospect} clicks on a @{Channel}
examples: The "Close your month faster" LinkedIn campaign creative

concepts.name: Customer Segment
concepts.description: A grouping of customers based on demographic attributes, never acquisition cohorts, per the IP's scope decisions.

concepts.name: Product
concepts.description: The SaaS application itself: the thing subscribers subscribe to.
concepts.definitionDifferentiator: is the SaaS application sold via @{Plan}s

coreBusinessEvents.name: Prospect Clicks on Ad
coreBusinessEvents.description: Funnel-top event: a prospect engages with a marketing creative on a channel.

coreBusinessEvents.name: Prospect Signs-up for Trial
coreBusinessEvents.description: Prospect provides their details and starts a time-boxed free evaluation.

coreBusinessEvents.name: Customer Activates Account
coreBusinessEvents.description: User confirms email, sets up their account, becomes addressable.

coreBusinessEvents.name: Customer Subscribes to a Paid Plan
coreBusinessEvents.description: Conversion event: a trial or prospect commits money to a plan.

coreBusinessEvents.name: Customer Upgrades or Downgrades their Subscription
coreBusinessEvents.description: Plan change that drives expansion or contraction MRR.

coreBusinessEvents.name: Customer Cancels their Subscription
coreBusinessEvents.description: Churn event: recurring revenue stops at the end of the current period.

coreBusinessEvents.name: Customer Renews their Subscription
coreBusinessEvents.description: Continuation of recurring revenue at the end of a billing period.

coreBusinessProcesses.name: Customer Acquisition
coreBusinessProcesses.description: The end-to-end process from a prospect clicking an ad through to becoming a paying customer. Owns Prospect Clicks on Ad → Signs-up for Trial → Activates Account → Subscribes to a Paid Plan.

coreBusinessProcesses.name: Subscription Lifecycle
coreBusinessProcesses.description: Managing a customer's subscription over time: renewals, upgrades, downgrades and cancellations. Owns Upgrades/Downgrades, Cancellations, and Renewals.

coreBusinessProcesses.name: Revenue Recognition
coreBusinessProcesses.description: Converting subscriptions, invoices, and payments into recognised recurring revenue figures (MRR, ARR, ARPU, NRR).

coreBusinessProcesses.name: Customer Retention
coreBusinessProcesses.description: Reducing churn and growing existing customers. Feeds NRR and expansion MRR calculations.

coreBusinessProcesses.name: Customer Segmentation
coreBusinessProcesses.description: Classifying customers by demographic attributes so revenue metrics can be sliced per segment.

domains.name: Marketing
domains.description: Ads, channels, and the acquisition funnel that brings prospects to the product.

domains.name: Sales
domains.description: Converting prospects to customers via plans and subscriptions.

domains.name: Customer Success
domains.description: Retention, expansion, and churn reduction across the subscription lifecycle.

domains.name: Finance
domains.description: Invoicing, payments and recognised revenue: the source of MRR, ARR, ARPU and NRR.

domains.name: Product
domains.description: The SaaS application itself: the plans, features and usage limits customers subscribe to.

scope.statement: Lead to revenue for a SaaS subscription company: from the first ad a prospect clicks, through trial and subscription, to the invoices, payments and recurring revenue that MRR, ARR and churn are counted from.

stories.name: A prospect becomes a paying customer
stories.text:
A prospect clicks on one of our ads on a channel like LinkedIn and signs up for a free trial. During the trial they set up their account and invite their team.
Before the trial ends they subscribe to a paid plan. From then on, every billing period produces an invoice, the customer pays it, and the subscription generates recurring revenue every month.

stories.name: A customer upgrades mid-period
stories.text: Halfway through a billing period, a customer moves from the Starter plan to the Pro plan. The subscription changes plan straight away, and the next invoice carries a prorated charge for the rest of the period. The discount they had on Starter no longer applies.

stories.name: A customer cancels at renewal
stories.text: A customer decides not to renew. They cancel before the end of the billing period, and the subscription stays active until the period ends. No new invoice is produced and the recurring revenue stops, but they are still a customer in our history.

businessQuestions.name: What is our Monthly Recurring Revenue by Plan?
How many Trials become a paid Subscription each month?
What is our monthly churn by Customer Segment?
What does it cost to serve each Customer?
